headline.note: Follow-up identifies Wollongong,Victoria Giants and New Zealand Breakers beforeCairns, Lander/Fairfieldstudy andKnoxplay. career_spells.evidence_note: Earlier umbrella described all pre-Cairns professional basketball. Named NBL spells now separated below; other overseas-club claims remain unverified and this remainder is not an additional continuous interval.
career_spells.counting_note: Paid professional work is indicated, but the employers, dates, hours and leave needed for a full-time calculation are unavailable.

career_spells.evidence_note: Official biographies say Smith signed with Cairns in 2005 and that his NBL career ended in 2009. His first speech identifies the 2008-09 season as his last and describes the club's insolvency, a 75 per cent pay cut and the end of his NBL employment. The club's official roster archive lists him in the 2005-06 through 2008-09 seasons. Party material describes this as five years, while the roster archive documents four playing seasons.
career_spells.counting_note: The paid professional relationship is supported, but season boundaries, off-season contractual periods, hours and leave are not published.

career_spells.employer: Office of Jim Turnour MP and office of Senator Jan McLucas
career_spells.role: Political staff member; exact titles not published
career_spells.evidence_note: In his first speech Smith said that after basketball he worked for then member for Leichhardt Jim Turnour and former senator Jan McLucas, and that McLucas gave him his first office job at age 30. The sequence, employing arrangements, exact dates, titles, hours and leave are not published.2009was inferred from basketball exit, not an office appointment date; removed. First-office age30does not independently resolve month or sequence.
career_spells.counting_note: Political staff employment is reported separately and excluded from public/private headline totals.

career_spells.evidence_note: Smith's official biography says that after basketball he worked for more than a decade in sport and recreation at state and local government levels. His first speech describes him as a sport and recreation officer but does not identify the state agency or boundaries.
career_spells.counting_note: Public control is supported, but the agency, exact dates, hours, leave and overlaps are unresolved.

career_spells.role: Club Development Officer; sport/recreation and community-facilities work
career_spells.evidence_note: Smith's official site identifies Council work delivering parks and playgrounds. Cairns Regional Council minutes attribute Cyclesport Precinct and Northern Beaches Youth Space reports to Matt Smith in March 2015; a Council committee paper attributes the 2017 Go Clubs report to him. A 2024 Prime Minister transcript records Smith saying he formerly worked for Council. The exact appointment and cessation dates are not published.17September2014report identifies Club Development Officer;11March2020minutes name his Active Living Cairns report.2015was an observation, not start; start nowunknown. These observations do not prove uninterrupted full-time service.
career_spells.counting_note: The local-government employer and work by March 2015 are supported, but start/cessation, hours, leave and the relationship to state-government service remain unresolved.

career_spells.evidence_note: Smith's first speech says he returned to the Queensland Basketball League, won a national championship with the Marlins and left elite basketball on his own terms in 2018. It does not supply seasons, remuneration, hours or whether this was employment alongside his sport-and-recreation work.
career_spells.counting_note: Paid employment is not established, so this athletic activity is excluded pending contract or payroll evidence.

career_spells.employer: Together Queensland, Industrial Union of Employees
career_spells.evidence_note: Smith's first speech says Together recruited him from a sport-and-recreation officer role and that he was happily organising for Together when approached to run for Parliament in 2024. His official site and Labor biography corroborate representing public-sector workers. Contemporary reporting identifies him as a Together Union organiser. The start date, exact 2025 cessation, hours, leave and candidate-period arrangements are not published.2025election is not evidence of union resignation; unsupported end removed.
career_spells.counting_note: Union employment is excluded from the public/private headline totals.

career_spells.employer: Community organisations in Far North Queensland
career_spells.evidence_note: The Labor biography and Smith's first speech describe free basketball clinics and occasional shoe drives during work travel. No employing entity or remuneration is identified.No evidence of2025cessation; removed snapshot-year boundary.
